Ishita: Pranav bhaiya, your demo was so clean today 😊 how did you plan it?
Pranav: I wrote the ending first, then worked backwards.
Ishita: ok I'm buying the same black notebook and copying your 6am schedule lol
Pranav: the 6am thing is only because my bus is early 😅 don't copy that
Ishita: haha fine. But the ending-first idea, that I'm keeping
Pranav: what do you want your demo to show?
Ishita: that our reminder tool is easy for my Nani to use
Pranav: then start from her taps. Ending first, but your ending
Ishita: ok. writing Nani's steps now

qa.q: What did Pranav do first when planning his demo?
qa.a: He wrote the ending first and then worked backwards.

qa.q: How does Ishita feel about Pranav's demo, and what does she decide to focus on?
qa.a: She admires it and is excited to copy his habits, but she settles on showing that the reminder tool is easy for her Nani to use.

qa.q: Why does Pranav's question about her demo help Ishita?
qa.a: It turns his method into her own goal, so she starts from her Nani's taps instead of copying his style. 🙂

qa.q: How might Pranav feel when Ishita says she will copy his notebook and schedule?
qa.a: He seems amused and a bit concerned, which is why he explains that the 6am thing is only because of his early bus.

grounding: A junior admires a senior and learns his way of thinking rather than copying his choices.

passage:
Twelve hours into the college hackathon, the hall was loud with fans and arguments, and Madhav's team had two hours left. All weekend he had been copying Trisha, the final-year student who had won last year: her dark-theme editor, her black coffee, even her way of saying "ship it".
At 2 a.m. his code broke. He ran to her table. "What would you do?"
She didn't take his laptop. "What's the error saying?"
"Null value in line 40."
"So where could it come from? Don't tell me my answer. Tell me yours."
He traced it back, slowly, while she asked questions. The bug was in his own data file.
"You've been copying my coffee," she said, grinning. "Copy how I ask questions instead. The coffee is terrible."
Madhav laughed and switched back to his light theme. They submitted at 3:58, two minutes early. He didn't win. But on the bus home he wrote her three questions in his notebook.

qa.q: How many hours into the hackathon was it?
Why had Madhav copied Trisha's editor, coffee and "ship it"?
qa.a: He admired her as last year's winner and wanted to be just like her.

qa.q: What did Trisha teach Madhav to copy instead?
qa.a: Her way of thinking: asking what the error says and where it could come from, rather than her style.

qa.q: How does Trisha see Madhav's imitation?
qa.a: With amusement; she grins and tells him to copy her questions, not her terrible coffee.

grounding: Shows admiring a senior who shows you the ropes, and learning their way of thinking rather than copying their style.

passage:
In her first month at the newspaper office on Park Street, Sharmila followed Irfan everywhere. He was the senior crime reporter who had broken the hospital fire story, and she wanted to be exactly him: the worn satchel, the three pens, the habit of calling sources from the stairwell.
When Irfan mentioned he had once left a full-time job to freelance, she started drafting her own resignation.
He found the draft on the shared printer. "Sharmila. Why?"
"Because it worked for you."
He sat her down in the canteen. "I left because my editor then was killing stories. Yours isn't. You'd be copying my decision without my reason." He pushed his notebook towards her. "Copy this instead. How I check a fact three ways before I file. How I listen to what a source doesn't say."
She read his notes for an hour. Then she shredded the draft. The next week she filed her first story, on school buses, a beat he had never covered, checked three ways.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila start drafting a resignation?
qa.a: She admired Irfan so much that she wanted to copy his choice to freelance simply because it had worked for him.

qa.q: What did Irfan tell Sharmila to learn from him instead?
qa.a: His thinking: checking a fact three ways and listening to what a source doesn't say, not his personal decisions.

qa.q: How did Irfan feel on finding the draft?
qa.a: Concerned; he saw she was copying his decision without his reason and took the time to explain.

grounding: Illustrates admiring a senior and learning his way of thinking instead of imitating his choices while ignoring one's own path.
